project_aim: Test whether host-resource presence translates to butterfly larval recruitment and adult reproduction only under appropriate phenology, host quality and enemy conditions, rather than treating each introduced plant distribution as equivalent fitness opportunity.

sources.scope: two Danaus species, native Asclepias curassavica versus introduced Calotropis procera; lab and field, bagged versus exposed
sources.strength: Real larval survivorship and development observations
sources.fatal_confounding: Field host species and field site are fully confounded: one site per host, and bagging also changes abiotic environment; cannot attribute host-type × bagging contrast purely to natural enemies.

sources.scope: 493 Danaus plexippus larvae over 2018-2019 in a common garden, 2 native Asclepias hosts × predator-exclusion versus exposed
sources.strength: Original individual identity, full adult emergence, repeated years, manipulated access to predators
sources.fatal_confounding: All plants are native to study region. This experiment supports host-identity×enemy-effect biological calibration, not native-vs-exotic fitness differences. Published paper itself already reports interactions.

sources.scope: monthly surveys of 15 East Bay garden routes 2022 and four repeated 2023 routes, with native/exotic milkweeds, monarch eggs, larvae, adults and OE
sources.strength: Observed real garden resources and three butterfly life stages at repeated spatial-temporal units
sources.fatal_confounding: Egg and larva counts are contemporaneous stage indices, not followed cohorts or survival probabilities; survey visibility, season, host type and weather vary jointly. A difference in separate model p-values does not test a stage interaction.

sources.scope: Phoebis rearing on cultivated native and alien Senna, plus parasitoid emergence, three Florida localities
sources.strength: Actual post-collection adult or parasitoid emergence on independently studied hosts
sources.fatal_confounding: 176 unresolved individual fates, inconsistent printed native parasitoid grand total, origin linked to species, site and repeated sampling. No cultivated-vs-wild treatment.
Successfully reared and documented taxa preferentially reported; all larval failures not guaranteed recorded. 9519 project-reported cases may not all be API-accessible.

guidance: Do not launch a separate full ecology manuscript using already-published examples alone.
Do not pool species/site experiments as if independent natural vs cultivated treatment replicates.

Prioritize original factorial 2026 dryad to check how much stage-based emergence differs under predator exclusion at equal host category; generalization to alien plants requires an additional paired experiment.
Prioritize route×month raw data from 2025 Figshare to test stage×non-native milkweed fraction at constant plant abundance/season/route, NOT by comparing two separate p-values.
Use 2023 repeated routes only as a limited temporal sensitivity, not an independent new city.
Raw downloads via Dryad/Figshare were not accessible in current analysis runtime as of this manifest; no unpublished results were inferred.
No automatic changes to main GEB manuscript.
